recentItems.title: How We’ll Actually Ditch Fossil Fuels — by the Numbers | Michael Liebreich | TED
recentItems.description:
Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing? Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again. Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required. The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected. (Recorded at TED Countdown: The Next Ten on October 15, 2026)

recentItems.title: "Deep listening” can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and divides #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Do you avoid talking to people you disagree with? Author and mediator Emily Kasriel thinks you should try it out. She explains why engaging with ideas that bother you is one of the most powerful things you can do — and presents her framework for “deep listening” that can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and political divides.

recentItems.title: The harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: When life gets uncertain, do you grip a little tighter? Neuroscientist Heather Berlin explores a surprising paradox: the harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way. Drawing on brain research and her own struggles with uncertainty, she shares practical ways to let go and make room for creativity, calm and flow.

recentItems.title: How to Teach a Robot to Dance | David Dobáš | TED
recentItems.description:
Teaching a robot to dance, move or even stand up used to take countless hours of training. Now, by simply recording a video, you can teach a robot a new skill in a fraction of the time, says roboticist David Dobáš. In a live demo with TED guest curator Bilawal Sidhu, Dobáš shows how advances in AI are transforming the way these humanoid machines learn — and proves it with a robot dance performance at the end.(Recorded at David Dobáš on April 17, 2026)

recentItems.title: The Couples Therapists Who Nearly Got Divorced | Harville Hendrix | TED
recentItems.description:
Couples therapists Harville Hendrix and Helen LaKelly Hunt spent decades teaching the world how to love well … even as their own marriage was falling apart. In this candid, funny talk, Hendrix recounts the yearlong experiment in listening that saved their relationship — and shows how any couple can break the cycle of criticism to rediscover joy. (Recorded at TED2026on April 15, 2026)

recentItems.title: Making the vaccine was never the hardest part— it was getting people to trust them #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: What good is a vaccine people don't trust? Immunologist and TED Fellow Kizzmekia Corbett co-developed the first COVID-19 vaccine to enter clinical trials — but she says making the vaccine was never the hardest part. The real obstacle is the gap between scientists and the people who have honest questions about the shots they're being asked to take. She shares a refreshing approach for taking on vaccine inquisitiveness and ensuring that humanity is ready for the next pandemic.

recentItems.title: The Science of Learning New Things | Tania Lombrozo | TED
recentItems.description:
With more information at our fingertips than ever before, learning should be getting easier ... yet the opposite seems to be true, says cognitive scientist Tania Lombrozo. Drawing on her research into how our minds understand and reason, she explores why more information can actually make learning harder — and shares the critical skill all great learners possess. (Recorded at TEDxNewEngland on October 30, 2025)

recentItems.title: Turns out, your group chat might be more powerful than you think. #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: Katie Paris quit her career in Washington, DC, to figure out how to make politics feel less like strangers shouting at each other and more like friends looking out for each other. In this practical talk, she reveals why conversations between real people can have a bigger impact on elections than anything millions of campaign dollars can buy.

recentItems.title: What People Living in Democracies Take for Granted | Leopoldo López | TED
recentItems.description:
Activist Leopoldo López learned the true value of freedom in a solitary confinement cell, when someone else decided if he would eat or see sunlight. In this searching conversation, he explains why democracy is losing ground across the globe, the state of Venezuela's transition after Maduro's capture and the 2026 earthquakes — and why he founded the World Liberty Congress to unite activists in the fight against autocracies. (This conversation, hosted by TED's Whitney Pennington Rogers, was part of an exclusive TED Membership event. recentItems.title: How Would You Design Your Dream City? | James Rojas | TED
recentItems.description:
Urban planner James Rojas has led hundreds of workshops where participants creatively design their ideal communities with small objects — and he's noticed that people of every age, income and background build strikingly similar places. Through play and storytelling, he shows how we can use our childhood memories and imaginations to shape the places we live and love. (Recorded at Play@TED on May 14, 2026)

recentItems.title: Photographer Platon says empathy is the secret ingredient for finding a human connection. #TEDTalks
recentItems.description: With his art, photographer Platon seeks to strip away assumptions and leave viewers with a window into his subject's character, filling our eyes with wonder and curiosity. Sharing extraordinary stories of what it's like to photograph some of the world's most prominent figures -- from Michelle Obama and Pussy Riot to Vladimir Putin and Muhammad Ali -- Platon captures the disarming power of empathy and human connection.
